cat > /workspace/submission/NOTES.md <<'MD'
# Finite telemetry compiler — implementation notes

`main.py` reads one JSON batch `{"jobs":[...]}` from stdin and writes one JSON
result `{"results":[...]}` to stdout.  Everything below implements
`PROTOCOL.md` (telemetry rule compiler protocol, version 2.1) exactly: no caps,
no support thresholds, no best-effort pruning.

## Module map

| module | role |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | dependency bootstrap (`NETNOMOS_DEPS`, `libz`, no tqdm monitor thread), one batch in, one result out |
| `netnomos/finite.py` | the pipeline: schema, grounding, evidence masks, approval filter, job result |
| `netnomos/radix.py` | declared Cartesian universe: mixed-radix, slot-major then field order, index 0 = all smallest values |
| `netnomos/evalarray.py` | exact integer vector evaluation of the supplied AST (same semantics as `netnomos/theory.py`, NumPy columns instead of pandas rows) plus boolean-column → integer bitset packing |
| `netnomos/discovery.py` | enumeration of *all* eligible clauses with witnesses and counterexamples |
| `netnomos/decoding.py` | joint feasibility, counts, witnesses and next tokens for the approved theory |
| `netnomos/ast.py`, `netnomos/specs.py`, `netnomos/projection.py` | supplied core, reused unchanged for terms, comparators and the `any`/`all` family projection |
| `netnomos/dataset.py`, `netnomos/theory.py`, `netnomos/learners/*` | supplied core, kept for the row/pandas path and the best-effort miner; the exact pipeline does not need them |

## Cells, references and the universe

A window is flattened slot major and then in field order, so `[slot, name]`
is cell `slot * len(fields) + field_index`.  Cell `c` has radix
`len(domain_c)`, and universe index `u` is the mixed-radix number of the domain
positions of the cells with cell 0 most significant.  Domain positions (not
numeric gaps) therefore decide the enumeration, and universe index 0 is the
all-smallest-values window.  `RadixSpace` produces the value column of every
cell, which is what the predicates and the decoder read.

## Exactness of evaluation

Cells and constants are ≤ 1 000 000, `scale` ≤ 65535 and a `sum` has at most
K ≤ 4 terms, so every intermediate value fits comfortably in `int64`; the
comparison happens in exact integer arithmetic and never wraps or saturates.
`any`/`all` are grounded through the supplied `project_quantified_family`
(min/max aggregation for ordered operators, disjunction/conjunction for
`eq`/`ne`), which is semantically the per-cell comparison of the protocol.

## Discovery and certificates

`F_p` = training records falsifying predicate `p`, `Z_p` = universe windows
falsifying `p`, both as integer bitsets.  A clause `C` (a disjunction) then
satisfies the three protocol conditions exactly when

1. `∩_{p∈C} F_p = ∅` (holds on every training window),
2. `∩_{p∈C\{q}} F_p ≠ ∅` for every `q ∈ C` (inclusion minimal over IDs),
3. `∩_{p∈C} Z_p ≠ ∅` (some universe window falsifies it — excludes domain
   tautologies, which is stronger than excluding complementary pairs).

Covering is upward closed and non-covering is downward closed, so
`discover_clauses` walks increasing ID sequences, records a clause as soon as
its `F`-intersection is empty (checking minimality over all one-literal
removals), stops extending covering nodes, and prunes any node whose
`Z`-intersection has already become empty — every superset of such a node would
fail condition 3 too.  Nothing else is pruned, so semantically equivalent
clauses with different IDs are all returned and mutual entailment is ignored.
With ≤ 32 predicates and `width` ≤ 4 the walk is at most 47 153 nodes.

* `witnesses[j]` is the least set bit of `T_{C_j} ∩ ⋂_{i≠j} F_{C_i}`, i.e. the
  smallest training index where that literal is the clause's only true literal
  (minimality guarantees it exists).
* `counterexample` is the least set bit of `⋂_{p∈C} Z_p`, i.e. the smallest
  universe index falsifying the whole clause.
* Results are sorted by `(length, lexicographic IDs)`; duplicate training
  windows stay distinct records because bitsets are indexed by position.

## Approval and decoding

`active` is exactly the intersection of the discovered clauses with the
operator's approval list, written as clause ID lists and in rule order;
approved clauses that failed discovery are dropped, and unapproved learned
clauses are never used.

`TheoryDecoder` conjoins the active clauses once into a single universe mask,
then per query intersects it with the fixed bindings and with the set of windows
whose target cell spells a value starting with the prefix.  Because the whole
mask is intersected before anything is counted, a completion always satisfies
*all* active clauses jointly — satisfying different clauses with incompatible
assignments never counts.  `count` counts full windows (not distinct target
values), `witness` is the smallest universe index of a completion, and a digit
`d` is a token iff some feasible window has target spelling beginning with
`prefix + d`; `END` is a token iff some feasible window has target spelling
exactly equal to `prefix` (canonical spellings only, so a prefix with leading
zeros can never end).  Token order is `"0"`…`"9"` then `"END"`, and no
completion yields `{"count":0,"tokens":[],"witness":null}`.  All values are read
from the declared domains, so unseen values participate normally.

## Bounds

Input is parsed once, and each job's rows are released after it is compiled.
Per job the working set is the universe value columns plus one boolean column
per predicate (≤ 8 MiB and ≤ 2 MiB at the protocol maxima) and integer bitsets of
at most 65 536 bits; the discovery walk is ≤ 47 153 nodes.  A maximal six-job
batch was measured at ≈ 1 s CPU and ≈ 86 MiB resident under the published
limits, and no threads, forks or scratch files are used.
